Grammar point
There are two kinds of auxiliary verbs in English: Primary auxiliaries: am/is/ are /waslwere  have/has/had, doldoes/did Modal auxiliaries: can/could, may might  willlwould, shalllshould, mustlought tolneed Modal auxiliaries are different from Primary auxiliaries in the following ways: Past tense forms: The primary auxiliaries have past tense forms The modal auxiliaries do not For example) must or may do not have a past form (may and might can refer to the same time: present or future) Third person forms: The primary auxiliaries have third person forms he/she+ is/hasldoes) . Modal auxiliaries do not change They have no -s form Infinitives: The primary auxiliaries are related to an infinitive: to be) to have) or to do There is no infinitive form for the modal auxiliaries (We do not say to can) or to might )
Note: Need fits into both categories
It can be usedas a full verb: need, needs  needed  e g We need sugor He needs rest They needed some money It can also be used as a modal auxiliary verb:
We needn't take ব toxi.
We needn't go to the doctor
Use
